extra.message: run_cmd() passes its argument directly to os.popen() which executes it via the shell. This function is called with attacker-controlled data from multiple GraphQL resolvers (system_diagnostics, system_debug, import_paste), enabling arbitrary OS command execution.

resolve_system_diagnostics passes the user-supplied 'cmd' GraphQL argument to helpers.run_cmd() (os.popen). In easy mode allowed_cmds() returns True for any command, allowing arbitrary OS command execution after a weak credential check.

resolve_system_debug concatenates the user-supplied 'arg' GraphQL argument into the command string 'ps {}' which is executed via os.popen(). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. ';id') to run arbitrary commands.

ImportPaste.mutate builds a curl command from user-supplied host/port/path/scheme arguments and runs it via helpers.run_cmd (os.popen). In easy mode strip_dangerous_characters returns the input unchanged, so shell metacharacters in these fields lead to arbitrary OS command execution.

ImportPaste.mutate fetches a fully user-controlled URL (scheme://host:port/path) using curl. There is no validation of the target host, allowing Server-Side Request Forgery to internal/cloud-metadata endpoints. The response body is returned to the attacker.

resolve_pastes builds a raw SQL fragment by string-formatting the user-supplied 'filter' argument directly into text("title = '%s' or content = '%s'"). This is passed to SQLAlchemy text() unescaped, allowing SQL injection (e.g. filter="x' OR '1'='1").

save_file concatenates the user-supplied 'filename' directly to WEB_UPLOADDIR without sanitization (open(WEB_UPLOADDIR + filename, 'w')). A filename containing '../' allows writing arbitrary files outside the upload directory. Reached via UploadPaste mutation.

get_identity decodes the JWT with verify_signature=False and verify_exp=False, then the 'identity' claim is trusted (resolve_me sets info.context.json['identity'] from it). An attacker can forge any identity (e.g. 'admin') to bypass authorization and read sensitive fields such as the admin password.

resolve_password gates returning the cleartext password solely on info.context.json['identity'] == 'admin', a value derived from an unverified JWT (see get_identity). Combined with the forgeable token, this exposes user passwords. Broken access control / sensitive data exposure.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: resolve_users returns user records (including password field) for any id with no authentication or authorization check, enabling IDOR enumeration of all user accounts.
resolve_delete_all_pastes deletes every paste in the database with no authentication or authorization, a destructive operation exposed to any anonymous caller.
EditPaste and DeletePaste mutations operate on any paste by id with no ownership or authentication check, allowing any user to modify or delete arbitrary pastes (IDOR).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: JWT_SECRET_KEY is hardcoded to the static value 'dvga'. Anyone knowing this trivial secret can forge valid signed JWT access/refresh tokens for any user.
Flask SECRET_KEY is hardcoded to the static value 'dvga', allowing forging/tampering of signed session cookies. This overrides the earlier random secret_key.
Default user accounts are seeded with hardcoded weak credentials (operator/password123, admin/changeme), providing guessable login credentials.

format_custom_error attaches full stack traces (traceback.format_stack), traceback.format_exc output, and source file paths into the GraphQL error 'extensions' returned to clients, leaking internal implementation details and aiding attackers.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: WEB_DEBUG defaults to True, enabling debug mode which can expose the Werkzeug interactive debugger and detailed error pages allowing potential remote code execution and information disclosure.

sys.setrecursionlimit(100000) drastically raises the recursion limit. Combined with GraphQL nested queries and no depth protection in easy mode, this facilitates resource-exhaustion / denial-of-service attacks.
resolve_pastes accepts a fully client-controlled 'limit' argument with no upper bound, allowing a client to request an arbitrarily large result set and cause resource exhaustion.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: The /graphql endpoint enables query batching (batch=True) with no authentication and weak per-request protections, allowing batched brute-force/enumeration attacks (e.g. against the Login mutation) and amplification.
